title: Exit quietly on closed stdout instead of panicking
description:
When stdout closes early (for example `jit gate status ... | head -2`), jit panics with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)` from the std print machinery.

## Background

Observed twice while piping gate output through `head` during an execution-lead session. A CLI whose primary consumer is an agent composing shell pipelines terminates pipelines early as a matter of course; a panic plus backtrace note on every truncated pipe is noise and reads as a crash.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A command whose stdout closes mid-write exits without a panic message or backtrace hint.
- [hard] REQ-02: The exit status in the broken-pipe case follows the conventional quiet-termination behavior for CLI tools rather than a panic exit.
- [hard] REQ-03: A regression test (or harness-level check) covers writing to a closed stdout.
